input.quote: This Agreement may not be assigned by either party, by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided that (a) M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement pursuant to a merger in which Customer is a party and as a result of which the surviving corporation becomes an Affiliate of another bank holding company, bank, savings and loan association or other financial institution having a capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000 so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with
input.rationale: § 22.4 fails the fallback on a material term. Consent and the "not unreasonably withheld" standard are present (fallback elements 3 and 4 are already met), but the successor rights are asymmetric: M&I "may freely assign" on a merger, reorganization or asset sale and to a successor of the M&I Data Services division, with no notice, while our only carve-out is a merger in which the survivor becomes an Affiliate of a financial institution with capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000 and § 21.11 is satisfied. That is not a mutual right to assign to a successor, and no successor assignment requires written notice. We therefore target the fallback: a mutual successor-assignment right exercisable on written notice, with consent (not unreasonably withheld) retained for all other assignments. Related points noted but not flagged here: § 21.11(B) caps M&I's post-change-of-control obligations at the pre-change entities and prior 3-month volumes plus 25% (a scope limit, not a Vendor termination or re-pricing right), § 21.11(A) puts new-Affiliate Conversion Expenses and to-be-agreed Conversion Fees on us, and § 11.3 ("Following Change in Control of Customer") is redacted and unreviewable — we reserve comment on any fee or right it carries.

ops.oldText: provided that (a) M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement pursuant to a merger in which Customer is a party and as a result of which the surviving corporation becomes an Affiliate of another bank holding company, bank, savings and loan association or other financial institution having a capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000 so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with and (b) M&I may freely assign this Agreement (i) in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities, or (ii) to any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division of M&I.
ops.newText: provided that either party may assign this Agreement without such consent, upon written notice to the other party, to a successor in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced the asymmetric carve-outs in § 22.4 with a mutual right to assign to a successor in a merger, reorganization or sale of substantially all assets on written notice, so our merger carve-out is no longer conditioned on the acquirer's size or on § 21.11, and M&I can no longer assign freely without notice. All other assignments continue to require the other party's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld; this is our fallback position. We note § 11.3 (Following Change in Control of Customer) is redacted and reserve comment on it.
proposal.summary: Make § 22.4 a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice, keeping consent (not unreasonably withheld) for all other assignments.
